text: Stavros chose Browser Use Cloud (3 Nov 2026) after comparing prices: $0.02/browser-hour, pay as you go. A remote browser is needed because Chromium cannot run in the plugin-runner image (missing system libraries, no root); the earlier local-Playwright plugin (STA-620, stavrobot/plugin-playwright) was cancelled and deleted for that reason.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Verified on 3 Nov 2026 with a real API key: a standalone V4 browser created with timeout: 1 and never stopped moved to status stopped by itself about 4 s after timeoutAt, cost $0.00033 (one browser-minute, the same as the billing minimum). The docs do not state this. The plugin relies on it as the backstop when the explicit stop call cannot run (for example the runner kills the process at its 300 s async limit). Because of the one-minute minimum, a browser left to time out costs about the same as one stopped early.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Profiles (Browser Use profileId for reusing logins) were considered and left out on 3 Nov 2026; Stavros agreed to stay stateless. Adding an optional profile_id config key later is small, but reusing logins also needs Browser Use's separate profile-sync workflow.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: On 5 Nov 2026 (STA-627) browse became an async tool so the page-load timeout could be 30 s: British Airways check-in pages failed at 15 s, and the plugin runner kills sync tools at 30 s, which cannot fit browser creation plus a 30 s load. Stavros chose async (results arrive as a follow-up message) over capping the load at about 20 s or raising the runner's sync timeout for all plugins. He also decided the timeouts stay fixed constants, not configuration.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
